input: Get a structural survey on the chimney breast

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The survey scope changes significantly depending on whether the goal is a full structural assessment, a pre-removal check, a safety inspection after damage, or a valuation-related report — each requires a different type of survey and surveyor.

Whether the chimney breast is in a mid-terrace, semi-detached, or detached property, and whether it spans multiple floors or has already been partially removed, directly affects the structural complexity and what the surveyor needs to assess.
Knowing whether the user needs to find and hire a surveyor from scratch, or already has one in mind, determines the first concrete action — searching for professionals vs. making a single call.
Budget sets the boundary on the type of surveyor (independent structural engineer vs. RICS-chartered surveyor) and the depth of report that is feasible.
Whether there is a deadline (e.g. tied to a house purchase, planned renovation, or a mortgage requirement) changes how urgently the surveyor needs to be booked and how the plan should be sequenced.

The desired output — a written report, a verbal assessment, a sign-off certificate for building control, or a quote for remedial work — determines what to ask the surveyor for and how to evaluate whether the task is truly done.

Whether the user wants a local independent structural engineer, a large firm, or a recommendation from a specific source (e.g. a trusted tradesperson or online directory) shapes how the search for a professional is conducted.

gold.taskTitle: Get a structural survey on the chimney breast
gold.taskDescription: Arrange for a structural survey to be carried out on a chimney breast, likely to assess its condition, safety, or suitability for removal or modification.

questions.title: What is the specific reason you need this survey?
questions.description: Understand the purpose — e.g. planning a removal, following damage, satisfying a mortgage lender, or a general safety check — to determine the right type of survey.

questions.title: What type of property is the chimney breast in?
questions.description: Establish the property type (e.g. mid-terrace, semi-detached, detached) and whether the chimney breast spans one or multiple floors, as this affects structural complexity.

questions.title: Do you already have a surveyor or engineer in mind?
questions.description: Determine whether the user needs to find and vet a professional from scratch or simply needs to contact someone they already have details for.

questions.title: What is your approximate budget for the survey?
questions.description: Clarify the budget to guide the choice between a structural engineer and a chartered surveyor, and to set expectations on report depth.

questions.title: Is there a deadline this survey needs to meet?
questions.description: Find out if the survey is tied to a time-sensitive event such as a house purchase, a renovation start date, or a building control submission.

questions.title: What output do you need from the surveyor?
questions.description: Clarify the required deliverable — e.g. a written structural report, a verbal assessment, a building control sign-off, or a remedial works quote — so the right brief can be given.

questions.title: How do you prefer to find and choose a surveyor?
questions.description: Understand whether the user wants to search a professional directory (e.g. IStructE, RICS), use a personal recommendation, or follow another preference for sourcing the right professional.
